The Sun on 29 September 2026

Real images from NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory, taken at 20:00 UTC. Each view shows gas at a different temperature, from the 5,800 K surface to 6-million-degree flare loops. Pick one from the ladder (or use the ← → keys).

Solar north is up; the Sun rotates from left (east) to right (west).

The week before, in 193 Å

One image every 3 hours for 7 days. Watch active regions ride across the disc as the Sun turns (once every 27 days as seen from Earth). Below, the X-ray output measured by GOES: every spike is a flare. Click the curve to jump to that moment.

GOES-18, 1–8 Å, 10-minute means. Dotted line: the week's most energetic flare, C2.4 from NOAA 4536 at 28 Sep 15:19 UTC. Letters are flare classes (each ten times the one below).

Data: SDO/AIA and SDO/HMI (NASA; JSOC, Stanford), GOES-18 XRS (NOAA SWPC and NCEI). Built by the Astrophysics Project Atlas, project F2.
